text:
tereza.pm: Quick sync: we need a crisp, customer-facing definition of the routing & isolation primitives that will land in our Q4 roadmap. Goal: unambiguous MVP scope + onboarding checklist. Who can help tighten acceptance criteria?

ishaan.eng: I can. Engineering cares about: deterministic routing rules (no random picks), performance envelopes per primitive, and a simple toggle to opt tenants into the new behavior. Need a concrete schema for the runtime to consume.

zoe.arch: Proposal: define three minimal primitives with clear semantics: 
- affinity: prefer previously-used backend for same tenant/session
- fallback: deterministic next-best region or capacity tier when preferred is unavailable
- quarantine: short-term eviction when tenant exceeds safety thresholds
These should map 1:1 to runtime hooks. Example policy document (human-first):
```yaml
policy_name: prod_affinity
primitive: affinity
preferences: [region-us-east-1, region-us-west-2]
strict: false  # if true, disallow fallback
ttl_seconds: 600
```
This keeps runtime logic simple and auditable.

mike.sre: Operational must-haves: per-tenant decision log (immutable), per-policy health metric, and a per-tenant emergency disable. Canary gate: <1% fallback rate on synthetic traffic for 7 days, and one successful controlled failover drill. Also need clear escalation runbooks.

ana.compliance: Additions from compliance: decision logs must include tenant_id (hashed ok), human-readable reason, timestamp, and region chosen. Audit export for regulated customers (90d default, encrypted at rest). Also surface residency hints so legal can verify data flow for specific tenants.

julia.sales: Customers want a negotiated migration SLA (X hours to cutover, Y hours rollback window) and a documented migration play. Also ask: can we guarantee a deterministic sequence for fallback so customers can prepare failover endpoints?

tereza.pm: Draft acceptance criteria (please challenge):
1) Machine-readable policy spec + 4 examples (single-region affinity, cross-region fallback, strict-residency, quarantine)
2) Runtime implements affinity/fallback/quarantine and exposes an opt-in per-tenant flag
3) Decision logs written to blob store with schema: policy_name, tenant_id_hash, input_hash, selected_backend, reason, latency_ms, token_estimate
4) Telemetry: 50th/95th/99th latency and token cost per policy path
5) Canary: 7-day synthetic + 1 dry-run failover, rollback automation tested
6) Customer onboarding packet + migration SLA template
7) Compliance-ready audit export for regulated customers

ishaan.eng: Suggest tightening #3: include model_family tag and policy_revision for debugging. Also set retention default 30d. For perf targets, we propose that affinity path must be within +10% of baseline 95th latency, fallback path allowed +30%.

zoe.arch: Add model gating: any model family with >2x variance on kernel perf must be flagged as non-affinity-safe until validated. Will add gating table to spec.

mike.sre: We'll own the alerting thresholds. Proposed alert: fallback_rate > 3% over 5m for production triggers paged incident. Also require daily agg report for fallback counts by tenant.

ana.compliance: Note: for customers in EU, strict residency=true must enforce no cross-region backup; document the enforcement behavior and the audit evidence we'll provide.

julia.sales: I'll map top 10 accounts to likely migration needs and share negotiation points (rollback window, SLA credits).

tereza.pm: Action owners & dates:
- Zoe: finish policy spec + gating table (ETA 2w)
- Ishaan: runtime schema + opt-in flag plan + perf targets (ETA 3w)
- Mike: telemetry contract + alerting + canary checklist (ETA 2w)
- Ana: compliance export requirements + residency enforcement doc (ETA 1.5w)
- Julia: customer migration ask list + sample SOW language (ETA 1w)
I'll assemble a one-pager that becomes the product RFC. Anything missing?

ishaan.eng: Risk: kernel/quantization changes could alter perf assumptions. Recommend we enumerate supported model families for MVP and make others opt-in later.

zoe.arch: Agreed. I'll include a "supported models" section and a simple JSON schema for policy objects.

mike.sre: Also schedule a staged cutover rehearsal in staging with test tenants after canary. I'm blocking capacity for that.

tereza.pm: Great. If no objections, I'll create the RFC and slot this for the roadmap triage next Thursday. :calendar:
